name: Superhuman
desc: Sells AI productivity software, including the Grammarly writing assistant, Superhuman email client and Coda documents, by subscription.
markets: Individuals and businesses worldwide use Grammarly; largest market is the United States, with enterprise sales growing internationally.
rationale: Mass-market consumer and business software brand with heavy advertising; F1 offers global reach and an enterprise hospitality platform.
changed: Grammarly acquired Superhuman in 2025 and renamed the company Superhuman later in 2025

name: Chainguard
desc: Sells hardened, minimal container images and open-source software libraries that reduce security vulnerabilities for enterprise development teams.
markets: Enterprise and public-sector customers, mainly in the United States; international customer spread not verified.
rationale: Venture-backed B2B security vendor with a developer audience; F1 fit is limited to enterprise hospitality and technology messaging.

name: Cohesity
desc: Sells data backup, recovery, ransomware protection and data management software to enterprises and government organisations worldwide.
markets: Enterprise and government customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; offices in India and Ireland.
rationale: Global enterprise software vendor selling to CIOs; F1 fits for B2B hospitality and data-resilience technology storytelling.
changed: Combined with Veritas Technologies' enterprise data protection business in 2024

name: Commvault
desc: Sells data protection, backup, recovery and cyber resilience software and SaaS to enterprises and governments.
markets: Enterprise and government customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, served directly and through partners.
rationale: Listed global B2B software company; F1 offers enterprise hospitality and a platform for its cyber-resilience message.

name: Cybereason
desc: Sells endpoint detection and response, extended detection and managed threat-hunting cybersecurity services to enterprises.
markets: Enterprise and managed-service customers in the United States, Europe, Israel and Asia-Pacific, including Japan.
rationale: Cybersecurity vendor whose rivals (CrowdStrike, Zscaler) sponsor F1; ownership change makes timing uncertain.
changed: LevelBlue agreed to acquire Cybereason in 2025; earlier planned merger with Trustwave did not complete

name: Luma AI
desc: Develops generative AI models for video and 3D content, including Dream Machine and Ray, for creators and enterprises.
markets: Creators and studios worldwide via subscriptions and API; Saudi investor Humain backs plans for compute in Saudi Arabia.
rationale: Consumer-facing AI video brand with Gulf backing; F1 content and Middle East races could showcase its creative tools.

name: Uniphore
desc: Sells an enterprise AI platform with conversational AI, speech analytics and AI agents for sales, marketing and customer service.
markets: Enterprise customers served from offices in the US, UK, Spain, Israel, UAE and India.
rationale: B2B AI vendor with India and Gulf presence; F1 could support enterprise hospitality, but brand budget is likely modest.

name: Wispr Flow
desc: Develops Wispr Flow, an AI voice dictation app that converts speech into text across macOS, Windows, iOS and Android.
markets: Individual professionals and teams buying subscriptions online; geographic split of users not verified.
rationale: Young consumer-productivity app; F1 is a large spend for its stage, though tech-savvy F1 audiences fit its users.

name: Lovable
desc: Provides an AI platform that builds web applications and websites from natural-language prompts for non-programmers and developers.
markets: Paying users worldwide, with the United States and Europe as main markets.
rationale: Fast-growing European AI brand chasing global consumers and businesses; F1 offers worldwide visibility and a technology showcase.

name: Aura
desc: Sells consumer subscriptions for identity theft protection, credit monitoring, antivirus, VPN and parental controls.
markets: Consumers and families mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Heavy US consumer advertiser; F1's growing US audience and three US races could suit brand campaigns.

name: EliseAI
desc: Sells conversational AI software that automates leasing, resident communication and scheduling for property managers and healthcare providers.
markets: Apartment operators and healthcare providers in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused B2B software firm with niche buyers; weak F1 fit beyond possible US race hospitality.

name: Enveda
desc: Biotech company using machine learning and metabolomics to discover small-molecule drugs from natural compounds for inflammatory diseases.
markets: Pre-revenue; research operations in the United States, with drug candidates in clinical development.
rationale: Pre-revenue drug developer with no consumer brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Oratomic
desc: Develops neutral-atom quantum computing hardware and error-correction technology, according to its Crunchbase profile.
markets: Pre-revenue; development operations in California only; no verified customers or expansion plans.
rationale: Early-stage quantum hardware developer with no product on sale and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Oxide Computer Company
desc: Builds rack-scale server computers with integrated firmware, hypervisor and software for running private clouds on premises.
markets: Enterprise and government customers mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Engineering-led hardware startup with little marketing culture; F1 fit limited to a data-centre technology story.

name: Replit
desc: Operates a browser-based software development platform with an AI agent that builds applications from plain-language prompts.
markets: Developers, students and businesses worldwide, with the United States as the largest market.
rationale: Fast-growing AI brand courting consumers and enterprises; F1 offers global visibility, as rival AI firms already sponsor teams.

name: Sigma Computing
desc: Sells cloud business intelligence software that lets users analyse data in cloud warehouses through a spreadsheet-like interface.
markets: Enterprise customers mainly in the United States; international footprint not verified.
rationale: B2B data-analytics vendor; F1 data storytelling fits, but brand budget and international reach are limited.

name: Skydio
desc: Manufactures autonomous drones and docking systems for defence, public safety and infrastructure inspection customers.
markets: Military, police, fire and utility customers in the United States and allied countries.
rationale: Defence-heavy drone maker with limited consumer marketing; F1 fit is weak beyond an autonomy technology story.

name: Spire Global
desc: Operates a constellation of small satellites and sells weather, aviation and space-based data and services to businesses and governments.
markets: Government and commercial customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; operations in the US, Luxembourg, UK and Singapore.

name: Upstage
desc: South Korean AI company selling Solar large language models and Document Parse document-processing AI to enterprises.

name: General Intuition
desc: AI research lab building foundation models and agents for spatial and temporal reasoning, trained on video game footage.
markets: Pre-revenue research lab in the United States; no verified customers or international plans.

name: Hyperscale Data
desc: Holding company owning AI data centre and bitcoin mining operations plus lending and other businesses.

name: Lila Sciences
desc: Builds AI models and autonomous laboratories to run experiments in life sciences, chemistry and materials science.
markets: Pre-revenue; research operations in the United States; partnerships not verified.

name: PaleBlueDot AI
desc: Provides cloud and AI computing services, according to its Crunchbase profile; customers and products are not confirmed.

name: Recursive
desc: Develops self-improving artificial intelligence systems, according to its Crunchbase profile; products and customers are not confirmed.

desc: Sells software testing automation and quality assurance products, including Tosca, to enterprises.
